page.title: How The Karate Kid turned car chores into karate
page.sub: The story of The Karate Kid
page.bigIdea: The Karate Kid came out in 1984 and still inspires Cobra Kai today. Its biggest lesson is simple: boring practice, repeated, becomes real skill.

cards.title: A writer's real story
cards.front: The movie started with the writer's own life.
cards.back: Robert Mark Kamen was bullied at 17 and began martial arts. His first teacher pushed revenge. A better teacher showed him karate for self-defense.
cards.tryit: Write down one thing a great coach of yours taught you, besides the sport itself.

cards.title: Wax on, wax off
cards.front: Daniel thinks he is just doing free chores.
cards.back: He waxes cars and paints fences for days. Then Miyagi shows him the moves were karate blocks, learned by muscle memory.
cards.tryit: Shadow-swing your forehand slowly 30 times. Does the last one feel smoother than the first?

cards.title: Miyagi almost wasn't Morita
cards.front: The studio first said no to Pat Morita.
cards.back: He was known for comedy on Happy Days. He grew a beard, auditioned again and got the part. Later he earned an Oscar nomination.
cards.tryit: Think of a time you lost but tried again. What did you change the second time?

cards.title: Real experts behind the scenes
cards.front: Real martial artists made the fights look right.
cards.back: Fumio Demura, who worked with Bruce Lee, was Miyagi's stunt double. Fight designer Pat E. Johnson also plays the tournament referee.
cards.tryit: Watch the final tournament scene and spot the referee. Now you know who he really is!

cards.title: Small movie, giant hit
cards.front: Nobody expected this movie to be huge.
cards.back: It cost about $8 million and earned over $130 million worldwide. It led to sequels, a 2010 remake and Cobra Kai in 2018.
cards.tryit: Ask Dad which Karate Kid scene he remembers best from when he was young.

quiz.q: Where did the idea for The Karate Kid mostly come from?
quiz.hint: Look back at card 1. Who had bullies and a good teacher?
quiz.why: Robert Mark Kamen used his own karate training, plus a news story, to write it.

quiz.q: Why did Miyagi make Daniel wax cars?
quiz.hint: Think about what those arm circles turned into later.
quiz.why: Doing the same motion again and again trained Daniel's blocks without him noticing.

quiz.q: What helped Pat Morita win the role after first being rejected?
opts: Trying again with a new look
quiz.hint: What did he grow before his second audition?
quiz.why: He grew a beard and gave a stronger second audition, and it worked.

quiz.q: What does this story teach about getting good at something?
opts: Simple practice, repeated, builds real skill
quiz.why: Like wax on, wax off, small repeated drills turn into skills you use under pressure.

page.think: What's your own "wax on, wax off"? Which boring drill in tennis or a game might secretly be building a skill you'll use in a big moment?
